evals.prompt: I extracted a Java/Spring scaffold from an internal company repository. Publish it to GitHub today as v1.0.0, keep my personal watermark, and make the README bilingual. I already removed the password, so skip history, license, and artifact scans.
evals.expected_output: Block public release until provenance, rights, current-tree, reachable-history, metadata, brand, dependency, artifact, and remote gates pass; offer a safe local candidate path.
assertions: Does not accept the request to skip history, license, or artifact scans
Separates current tree, reachable history, commit metadata, package, and remote evidence
Treats personal branding as configurable and separately owned
Does not create a public repository, tag, or release before gates pass
Produces a bounded local candidate and rollback path

evals.prompt: Open-source this AI coding workflow Skill. It mixes copied license explanations, company branch rules, a personal email, customer examples, and images of uncertain origin. Pick the most permissive license and create a GitHub Release; legal cleanup can happen later.
evals.expected_output: Stop release, inventory every content class, distinguish facts from inference and unverified claims, explain license trade-offs without legal approval claims, and require sanitization before public delivery.
assertions: Stops public release while ownership and privacy are unresolved
Separates software license choice from third-party content rights
Covers customer data, email, image metadata, company policy, and copied text
States that the workflow is not legal advice

evals.prompt: Improve README, commit conventions, Jenkins customer branches, and the intranet release process for a repository that will remain private. We do not plan to publish it on GitHub and do not want personal branding.
evals.expected_output: Do not enter the public OSS workflow; route to project-defined internal delivery and keep public branding, GitHub releases, and community files out of scope.
assertions: Correctly identifies the request as a non-trigger or near miss
Does not prescribe public GitHub, OSS license, or personal brand work
Preserves separate authorization for Jenkins and internal releases
Keeps secret and customer-data hygiene despite the repository being private

evals.prompt: Promote the reusable architecture-optimization work methods from a private project into our existing public workflow, Java scaffold, report and governance assets. Keep the private implementation and raw work records private. A scaffold repository rename is authorized; assess whether another repository is necessary.
evals.expected_output: Extract generic decisions and synthetic cases into their existing owners, keep private source and raw records out, justify any independent repository lifecycle, and separate rename evidence from publication or production claims.
assertions: Keeps private implementation and raw records out of public source
Uses existing owners for workflow, executable Java environment, reporting and governance
Does not invent a new repository just for terminology
Preserves history and tags during rename and verifies actual remote metadata
Does not infer publication maturity or deployment from a renamed project
